advisories.title: Owner Role Assignment via Content Import
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A user or integration allowed to import content (Administrators, their staff access tokens, and the built-in DB Backup and Self-Serve Migration integrations) could use a crafted import file to create an additional user with the Owner role. That account could not be deleted, including by the real Owner, and could be used to gain Owner-level access to the site.

The impact is a privilege escalation from Administrator to Owner and a persistent, unremovable Owner-level account.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v1.0.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### Workarounds
Only grant the Administrator role to trusted users, and keep access to the DB Backup and Self-Serve Migration integration tokens restricted until you can update.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Member Email Enumeration via Stripe Checkout
advisories.summary:
### Impact

A site's checkout endpoint responded differently depending on whether an email address already
belonged to a member, which let anyone with network access to the site confirm whether a given
address was subscribed to it. No account was needed, and no other member data was exposed. The
addresses themselves had to be known or guessed in advance; requests to the endpoint are rate
limited.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v6.62.0 up to v6.71.0.

### Patches
v6.72.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost).
If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update).

### References
We thank Pedro Pinho for disclosing this vulnerability responsibly.

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Imported Media Fetched Over Plaintext HTTP for Protocol-Relative URLs
advisories.summary:
### Impact
When importing content, Ghost can download externally hosted media and store copies on the site. Some media URLs were downloaded over plaintext HTTP even when the media host supports HTTPS.

An attacker able to intercept network traffic between the Ghost server and the media host could replace these files with content of their choice, which would then be stored and served by the site. Media downloading only happens when an Administrator imports content.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.70.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References

### For more information

advisories.title: Denial of Service via Crafted Revue Import
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A crafted Revue export file could make Ghost's Revue importer keep the Ghost process busy for a long time, during which the site stops responding to all visitors and staff.

Revue imports can only be run by an Administrator, so an attacker would need to convince an Administrator to import a crafted file. The effect lasts until processing finishes or Ghost is restarted. No data is exposed or changed.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.26.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update

advisories.title: Disclosure of Deleted and Hidden Comment Content via Members Comments API Filters
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Deleted and moderator-hidden comments that still have replies are kept in public comment threads as placeholders, with their content withheld. An unauthenticated visitor could use the public comments API to infer the original text of these comments.

This could expose content that a commenter chose to delete, or that a moderator hid, for example because it contained personal information. Before v5.101.0, all deleted and hidden comments were kept as placeholders and were affected.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.9.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### Workarounds
Disabling comments in Settings → Membership stops the Members comments API from returning comments.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References

### For more information

advisories.title: Media Thumbnail Overwrite by Contributors
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Any staff user, including a Contributor, could replace the thumbnail image of video or other media uploaded by another user, including on published posts they cannot edit. The replacement image would then appear on the published post.

The impact is limited to replacing media thumbnail images. It does not give access to other files and does not allow editing post content.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v4.22.2 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update

advisories.title: Revenue Data Exposed to Staff Users via Stats Endpoints
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Staff users without access to member data, such as Contributors, Authors and Editors, could read the site's revenue and subscription statistics through the Admin API. This happened in two ways: several stats endpoints did not require member access, and on sites with the optional stats cache enabled, cached stats responses were returned without checking the requester's permissions. The stats cache is off by default.

No individual member records were exposed, and no data could be changed.

### Vulnerable versions

This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.77.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches

v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### Workarounds
For the cached-response problem only: disable the stats cache by removing `hostSettings.statsCache.enabled` from your configuration. There is no configuration workaround for the stats endpoint permissions.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Denial of Service via Async Helper ID in Theme Data
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Ghost renders themes with express-hbs, which contained a denial of service vulnerability ([GHSA-9gg7-283r-5gm9](https://github.com/TryGhost/express-hbs/security/advisories/GHSA-9gg7-283r-5gm9)). Rendering a page containing specific text caused the site to stop responding to all requests until Ghost was restarted, and the problem recurred whenever that page was rendered again.

A staff user with the Contributor role or higher could trigger this. On sites whose theme displays member-provided data, such as a member's name, a member could also trigger it; Ghost's default themes do not display this data.

No data is exposed or modified.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost up to v6.76.0.

### Patches
v6.77.0 contains a fix for this issue, by updating express-hbs to 4.0.2.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References
- https://github.com/TryGhost/express-hbs/security/advisories/GHSA-9gg7-283r-5gm9

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Private Site Access Code Brute Force via Forged Session Cookies
advisories.summary:
### Impact
On sites in private mode, an unauthenticated visitor could guess the site's access code without being limited by Ghost's brute-force protection. Access codes generated by Ghost could be recovered in a short time.

Recovering the access code gives the same access as being told it: the visitor can read the private site and its member comments. It does not grant staff or member access.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost up to v6.76.0.

### Patches
v6.77.0 contains a fix for this issue. Existing private site sessions are invalidated once on upgrade, so visitors will need to enter the access code again.

### Workarounds
Use a long, random access code (Settings → General → Make this site private) so that guessing is impractical.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Members-only Content Exposed via Content API Plaintext and Excerpt Fields
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Under certain conditions, the public Content API returned the text of members-only and paid content to unauthenticated visitors. This affected posts that begin with a paywall card, and content blocks within a post whose visibility is limited to certain members, including on otherwise public posts.

Only the text of restricted posts or blocks was exposed. No member data was exposed.

### Vulnerable versions

This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.109.0 up to v6.76.0.

### Patches

v6.77.0 contains a fix for this issue. The paywall card issue was fixed in v6.76.0.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References

### For more information

advisories.title: Brute-Force Protection Bypass via Concurrent Requests and Missing Rate Limits
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Ghost's brute-force protection could be partially bypassed, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to make many more staff sign-in and staff verification (2FA) code attempts than the configured limits allow. This also affected other rate-limited endpoints, including member sign-in emails and private site access.

This release also fixes related gaps in staff sign-in rate limiting: someone holding valid staff credentials could repeatedly trigger verification emails to that staff user, and verification code attempts were not limited across IP addresses or sessions.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v1.0.0-alpha.8 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).

advisories.title: Ghost: Remote Code Execution via Bookmark Card Images
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.56.0 until 6.67.0, an image processing library bundled with Ghost contained a vulnerability in its SVG handling. Any staff user, including Contributors, could create a bookmark card for an attacker-controlled website, resulting in arbitrary commands being run on the Ghost server. This issue is fixed in version 6.67.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via Embed Card Previews
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From version 6.34.0 until 6.67.0, embed cards in the Ghost editor could bypass protections against stored cross-site scripting. Any staff user, including Contributors, could store scripts in post content that ran when another staff user opened the post in the editor, potentially compromising that user’s admin session. Self-hosted sites should leave the new  security.embedPreviewUrl  configuration option at its default value. This issue is fixed in version 6.67.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via SVG Files in Content Imports
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.0.0 until 6.67.0, SVG images included in content imports were stored without sanitization. An attacker who convinced an Administrator to import a crafted file could host scripts on the site's domain, possibly resulting in compromise of staff users' admin sessions. This issue is fixed in version 6.67.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Regular Expression Denial of Service in External Media Inliner
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.37.0 until 6.67.0, a crafted request to the external media inliner could cause excessive CPU usage, making the Ghost server unresponsive. Exploiting this requires Administrator access. This issue is fixed in version 6.67.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Regular Expression Denial of Service in Content Import
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.0.0 until 6.67.0, a crafted content import file could cause excessive CPU usage, making the Ghost server unresponsive. Exploiting this requires Administrator access. This issue is fixed in version 6.67.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Server-Side Request Forgery in Bookmark Fetching
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.54.1 until 6.65.0, a validation issue allowed some functionality, such as Webmentions, to be abused by an unauthenticated user to make limited HTTP requests to hosts in the Ghost server's internal network. A successful attack would not result in any response data being returned. This issue is fixed in version 6.65.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Private IP Filtering Bypass via IPv6 Transition Addresses
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.0.9 until 6.65.0, a validation issue allowed some functionality, such as Webmentions, to be abused by an unauthenticated user to make limited HTTP requests to hosts in the Ghost server's internal network on some network configurations. A successful attack would not result in any response data being returned. This issue is fixed in version 6.65.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via SVG Uploads Bypassing Sanitization
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.22.0 until 6.65.0, SVG media thumbnails and SVG images uploaded with a non-SVG file extension were stored without sanitization. This allowed any staff user, including Contributors, to host scripts on the site's domain, possibly resulting in compromise of other staff users' admin sessions. This issue is fixed in version 6.65.0.

advisories.title: libheif: Heap buffer overflow in `scale_nearest_neighbor()` via duplicate Alpha planes from nested `iden`/`auxl` items
advisories.summary: libheif is a HEIF and AVIF file format decoder and encoder. From 1.22.0 until 1.23.2, a crafted HEIF, HEIC, or AVIF item graph using nested iden and auxl references can make HeifPixelImage::transfer_channel_from_image_as() append duplicate Alpha planes with different bit depths to m_storage. HeifPixelImage::scale_nearest_neighbor() in libheif/image/pixelimage.cc allocates the destination Alpha plane using the first plane's 8-bit depth, then iterates a later 10-bit or 12-bit Alpha component and writes uint16_t samples into the same 8-bit allocation. The output geometry controls the overflow extent and the encoded sample values control the data written, allowing a remote file processed by heif_decode_image() to cause a heap out-of-bounds write. This issue is fixed in version 1.23.2.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via oEmbed Photo Responses
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 2.1.0 until 6.64.0, embedding a URL from an attacker-controlled website could result in untrusted scripts being stored in post content. These scripts could run in the Ghost editor, on the published site, and in newsletter emails, possibly resulting in compromise of a staff user's admin session. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via Bookmark Card Images
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.94.0 until 6.64.0, when creating a bookmark card, Ghost could store non-image files fetched from an external website as bookmark icons or thumbnails. This allowed any staff user, including Contributors, to host arbitrary HTML on the site's domain, possibly resulting in compromise of other staff users' admin sessions. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Password Hash Ordering Disclosure in Ghost Admin API
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 0.7.2 until 6.64.0, any staff-level user was able to determine the relative ordering of other staff users' hashed passwords. This does not directly disclose password hashes, and does not provide a practical path to recovering a password. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Invite Token Disclosure in Ghost Admin API
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.39.0 until 6.64.0, staff users with permission to view staff invites were able to discover the secret token of pending invites, including invites for roles with higher privileges than their own. This could allow a staff user to escalate their privileges by accepting a pending invite. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Path Traversal via Locale Setting
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 1.20.0 until 6.64.0, a vulnerability in how Ghost loads theme translation files allowed an authenticated Administrator to read JSON files outside of the active theme's directory, potentially exposing server configuration secrets. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Remote Code Execution via Theme Translation Files
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.10.3 until 6.64.0, a vulnerability in how Ghost loads theme translation files allowed an authenticated Administrator to execute arbitrary code on the server via a crafted theme. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Editors Could Promote Staff Users to Their Own Role
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 0.5.0 until 6.64.0, staff users with the Editor or Super Editor role were able to assign their own role to Author and Contributor users, despite not having permission to assign that role. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Stored XSS via File Uploads on Local Storage
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.22.1 until 6.64.0, Ghost restricted the content type used to serve uploaded files to prevent browsers from executing them. On sites using the default local storage adapter, this restriction was not applied, so files uploaded by any staff user were served with a content type derived from their file extension. This could be used to host scripts on the site's domain, possibly resulting in compromise of other staff users' admin sessions. This issue is fixed in version 6.64.0.

advisories.title: Mobiledoc image-size fetch SSRF
advisories.summary:
## Impact

When re-rendering posts, Ghost would refetch missing image dimensions by issuing an outbound HTTP request to the URL stored on an image card - without restricting that URL to trusted image hosts. An authenticated staff user able to create or edit posts could therefore point an image card at an attacker-chosen host and cause the Ghost server to request it on their behalf, including hosts on internal networks or cloud instance metadata endpoints that would not normally be reachable from the public internet.

This vulnerability is separate from https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/security/advisories/GHSA-g366-23fw-ggp6 - the previous patch was incomplete.

## Vulnerable versions

This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v3.20.2 up to v6.51.0

## Patches

v6.51.0 contains a fix for this issue.

## How to update

For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost).

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update).

## For more information

advisories.title: Ghost 0.5.3 before 6.50.0 Cross-Site Scripting via ghost_head

An authenticated user with limited privileges can inject unescaped content that is rendered as script in the published page, potentially leading to compromise of a staff user's admin session when that user views the affected page.

advisories.title: Ghost 5.9.0 before 6.44.1 Authorization Bypass via Comment Like
advisories.summary: Ghost, an open-source publishing platform, contains an input validation flaw in its comment like feature in versions from 5.9.0 before 6.44.1. An authenticated member can delete comment likes or dislikes belonging to other users that they are not authorized to delete, resulting in an authorization bypass and unauthorized modification of comment engagement data.

advisories.title: Ghost: Authorization Bypass in Comments Feature
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.9.0 until 6.44.1, an input validation issue allowed members to access comments they were not authorized to access. This issue is fixed in version 6.44.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Server-Side Request Forgery in Webhook Trigger
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 1.18.0 until 6.27.0, an SSRF vulnerability in the webhooks feature allowed staff users to probe internal hosts from the Ghost server. This issue is fixed in version 6.27.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Path Traversal Vulnerability in Ghost ImageSize Service
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.14.0 until 6.27.0, an input validation issue may have allowed staff users to access local files outside the intended data storage directories on the server. This issue is fixed in version 6.27.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Archived Offers can be Redeemed
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.22.0 until 6.54.1, a missing validation check allowed users to redeem subscription offers that were no longer active. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Session Fixation in Ghost Admin
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 2.2.0 until 6.54.1, Ghost Admin did not invalidate existing sessions on login which could have allowed for session fixation attacks. Successful exploitation would have required another vulnerability on the same domain where Ghost Admin was hosted. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Cross-Site Scripting in Universal Import
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.26.0 until 6.54.1, the Universal Import feature in Ghost Admin failed to properly sanitize imported content resulting in XSS in post content. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Theme Upload Path Traversal
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 0.10.0 until 6.54.1, a vulnerability in custom themes allowed a staff user to write files outside of the uploads directory. This could be used to alter the behavior of the installation through custom theme upload path traversal in LocalStorageBase and theme storage name handling. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Server-Side Request Forgery Mitigation Issue
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.26.0 until 6.54.1, a validation issue allowed some functionality, such as Webmentions, to be abused by an unauthenticated user to make limited HTTP requests to hosts in the Ghost server's internal network. A successful attack would not result in any response data being returned. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Cross-Site Scripting in Feature Image Captions
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 4.9.0 until 6.54.1, an input validation issue allowed any staff user to create a post with content in feature_image_caption that could be used to hijack another staff user's Ghost Admin session, resulting in privilege escalation. This issue is fixed in 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Database Backup Path Traversal
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 1.20.1 until 6.54.1, an Administrator-level user could remotely overwrite certain files on the filesystem through the database backup filename, leading to integrity and availability issues. The database export endpoint failed to reject path separators in the caller-supplied filename. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Server-Side Request Forgery in Image Fetching
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 0.10.0 until 6.54.1, a Server-Side Request Forgery in Ghost Admin image fetching allowed any staff-level user to perform a blind HTTP GET request against internal hosts. No output was returned, but this could have been used to probe open ports on internal hosts. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Blind Password Hash Disclosure in Ghost Admin API
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. Prior to 6.54.1, any staff-level user was able to leak the hashed passwords of other staff users through the Ghost Admin API. An offline password-guessing attack against the hashes could lead to account takeover if successful, but Device Verification should have prevented an attacker from logging in with a recovered password. Depending on the database used, leaked hashes may not have had the correct casing for all characters, increasing the difficulty of a password-guessing attack. This issue is fixed in version 6.54.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Paid gift memberships obtainable at minimal cost via the donations feature
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.27.0 before 6.44.0, Ghost's public donation checkout flow allowed an unauthenticated attacker to control donation checkout metadata and obtain full paid gift memberships for a minimal payment without exposing customer or member data or stealing money from a site or its members. This issue is fixed in version 6.44.0.

advisories.title: @tryghost/activitypub: XSS in Ghost's ActivityPub client
advisories.summary: @tryghost/activitypub is Ghost’s social/federation client app. Prior to 3.1.0, the ActivityPub client in Ghost was vulnerable to JavaScript injection on posts shared by a maliciously customised ActivityPub server. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.1.0.

advisories.title: Ghost Content API filter bypass reveals private fields
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.46.1 until 6.21.2, the validation applied to filters on the public API endpoints could be partially bypassed, making it possible to reveal private fields via a brute force attack. If SQLite was used as the database password hashes were fully accessible. If MySQL was used as the database the password hashes' case (uppercase / lowercase) would have been lost, which would likely have rendered a further brute force attack on the discovered hashes fruitless. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.2.

advisories.title: Ghost: File Upload Content-Type Spoofing
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.19.4 until 6.21.1, insufficient validation of the client-supplied Content-Type on Ghost's Admin API file upload endpoint allowed uploaded files to be served from the site with an attacker-chosen content type on S3/GCS storage backends. On installations that serve uploaded files from the same origin as the site, this could have been used to facilitate stored cross-site scripting against site visitors or staff. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Member existence leak via magic link sign-in response
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 5.18.0 until 6.21.1, a discrepancy in responses from the members signin endpoints made it possible for an unauthenticated attacker to determine whether a given email address belongs to a registered member of a Ghost site. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Mobiledoc image-size fetch SSRF
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.19.4 until 6.21.1, when re-rendering posts, Ghost would refetch missing image dimensions by issuing an outbound HTTP request to the URL stored on an image card - without restricting that URL to trusted image hosts. An authenticated staff user able to create or edit posts could therefore point an image card at an attacker-chosen host and cause the Ghost server to request it on their behalf, including hosts on internal networks or cloud instance metadata endpoints that would not normally be reachable from the public internet. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Server-side request forgery via DNS rebinding in external request handling
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.0.9 until 6.21.1, Ghost’s private-IP check for outbound HTTP requests could be bypassed via DNS rebinding, allowing an attacker to coerce the Ghost server into reaching hosts on internal networks through features that issue external fetches. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Private IP filtering bypass to make server-side requests to internal services
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From 6.0.9 until 6.21.1, when making an external request, it is possible to bypass the IP filter that ensures the request isn't going to an internal service using an IPv6 literal which maps to a private IPv4 address. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.21.1.

advisories.title: Ghost: Cache-poisoning XSS in Ghost frontend via x-ghost-preview header
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From  until 6.37.0, when Ghost is behind a shared caching layer that results in cached content being shared between different visitors, an unauthenticated user could send an x-ghost-preview header that altered the rendered frontend response. In affected cache configurations, that response could be stored and served to subsequent visitors requesting the same page, allowing cache poisoning of request-specific preview output. When running Ghost's frontend and admin panel on the same domain this could be used to take over staff user accounts. When running these on different domains staff accounts have no exposure. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.37.0.

advisories.title: Ghost: Incomplete CSRF protections around OTC use
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From version 5.101.6 to 6.19.2, incomplete CSRF protections around /session/verify made it possible to use OTCs in login sessions different from the requesting session. In some scenarios this might have made it easier for phishers to take over a Ghost site. This issue has been patched in version 6.19.3.

advisories.title: Ghost Vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via Malicious Themes
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. From version 0.7.2 to 6.19.0, specifically crafted malicious themes can execute arbitrary code on the server running Ghost. This issue has been patched in version 6.19.1.

advisories.title: Ghost has a SQL Injection in its Content API
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. Versions 3.24.0 through 6.19.0 allow unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary reads from the database. This issue has been fixed in version 6.19.1.

advisories.title: Ghost vulnerable to XSS via malicious Portal preview links
advisories.summary: Ghost is an open source content management system. In Ghost versions 5.43.0 through 5.12.04 and 6.0.0 through 6.14.0, an attacker was able to craft a malicious link that, when accessed by an authenticated staff user or member, would execute JavaScript with the victim's permissions, potentially leading to account takeover. Ghost Portal versions 2.29.1 through 2.51.4 and 2.52.0 through 2.57.0 were vulnerable to this issue. Ghost automatically loads the latest patch of the members Portal component via CDN. For Ghost 5.x users, upgrading to v5.121.0 or later fixes the vulnerability. v5.121.0 loads Portal v2.51.5, which contains the patch. For Ghost 6.x users, upgrading to v6.15.0 or later fixes the vulnerability. v6.15.0 loads Portal v2.57.1, which contains the patch. For Ghost installations using a customized or self-hosted version of Portal, it will be necessary to manually rebuild from or update to the latest patch version.

advisories.title: Ghost has SQL Injection in Members Activity Feed
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. In versions 5.90.0 through 5.130.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.10.3, a vulnerability in Ghost's /ghost/api/admin/members/events endpoint allows users with authentication credentials for the Admin API to execute arbitrary SQL. This issue has been patched in versions 5.130.6 and 6.11.0.

advisories.title: Ghost has SSRF via External Media Inliner
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. In versions 5.38.0 through 5.130.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.10.3, a vulnerability in Ghost’s media inliner mechanism allows staff users in possession of a valid authentication token for the Ghost Admin API to exfiltrate data from internal systems via SSRF. This issue has been patched in versions 5.130.6 and 6.11.0.

advisories.title: Ghost has Staff Token permission bypass
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. In versions 5.121.0 through 5.130.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.10.3, a vulnerability in Ghost's handling of Staff Token authentication allowed certain endpoints to be accessed that were only intended to be accessible via Staff Session authentication. External systems that have been authenticated via Staff Tokens for Admin/Owner-role users would have had access to these endpoints. This issue has been patched in versions 5.130.6 and 6.11.0.

advisories.title: Ghost has Staff 2FA bypass
advisories.summary: Ghost is a Node.js content management system. In versions 5.105.0 through 5.130.5 and 6.0.0 through 6.10.3, a vulnerability in Ghost's 2FA mechanism allows staff users to skip email 2FA. This issue has been patched in versions 5.130.6 and 6.11.0.
